Title: Mesaionike Bibliotheke (Bibliotheca Graeca Medii Aevi), tomos 3: Kaisarios Dapontes, Sergios Makraios, Anastasios Gordios, Demetrios Prokopiou, Alexandros Tyrnavites, catalogues of unpublished letters, patriarchal documents, a catalogue of martyrs (Greek)
Creator: Konstantinos N. Sathas (editor); texts by Kaisarios Dapontes (Historikos Katalogos), Sergios Makraios (Hypomnemata ekklesiastikes historias), Anastasios Gordios, Demetrios Prokopiou and Alexandros Tyrnavites, with Sathas's own regesta of patriarchal documents and catalogue of the martyrs from 1453 to 1811
Publisher: Typois tou Chronou, Venice
Publication Date: 1872
Rights: Public Domain (printed 1872)
Language: ell
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_C6PaY5ZGN5UC, file bub_gb_C6PaY5ZGN5UC_djvu.txt (National Library of Naples copy, Google scan), fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, one-world agent for Orthodoxy under the Ottomans), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: licenceurl Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from long s normalised to s (0 occurrences). Rights basis restated: a book printed at Venice in 1872 is public domain by date.
Content note: Volume 3 of Sathas's series (the host catalogue does not number it; the title page reads 'TOMOS G'). The Google boilerplate heads the file as Greek-script noise. Order in the file: title page (about line 20-45), Sathas's prologue (from line 69), Dapontes's Chronographos (section A, running heads 'CHRONOGRAPHOS' and 'KAISARIOU DAPONTE', from about line 4438 to 8057), Dapontes's Historikos Katalogos andron episemon, 1700-1784 (section B, from line 8058 to about 13523), Makraios's Hypomnemata ekklesiastikes historias (from 13524), Gordios (from 22595), Prokopiou (from 25243), Tyrnavites and the catalogues of unpublished letters (between Prokopiou and the patriarchal documents), the patriarchal documents (Sathas's regesta of acts from 1568 onward, from line 27987), and the catalogue of those martyred for the Christian faith from the fall of Constantinople to 1811 (from line 30477, one line per martyr with date and place, compiled by Sathas from the Neon Martyrologion of 1799 and the Neon Leimonarion of 1819). OCR sampled at five points: the Greek body is readable with ordinary accent errors; running heads and the Google notices are garbled. The eighteenth-century authors are a late witness to this world's window; the martyr catalogue and the regesta are the editor's apparatus, not the documents' own text.
